[untitled BTM module] These genes form a brake system on leukocyte activation, tuning how strongly lymphocytes and myeloid cells respond to antigen receptor, Toll-like and cytokine receptor engagement. Restraint of this kind sets thresholds for activation, prevents autoimmunity and chronic inflammation, and is also what tumours exploit to blunt T cell responses, making several members attractive immunotherapy targets.

members: [untitled BTM module] These genes outline the terminal stages of erythroid differentiation, in which a committed progenitor remodels its membrane and cytoskeleton, condenses and expels its nucleus, and emerges as a deformable red cell able to survive repeated passage through capillaries and the spleen. Structural components dominate: beta-spectrin builds the membrane skeleton beneath the lipid bilayer, pleckstrin-2 and cortactin drive the actin rearrangements required for enucleation and cell shaping, and XK forms a disulphide-linked complex with the Kell glycoprotein at the erythrocyte surface.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the erythroid-megakaryocytic branch of hematopoiesis, the programme by which bone marrow progenitors commit to making red cells and platelets rather than lymphoid or granulocytic fates. Its transcriptional core is a TAL1-GFI1B axis that drives erythroid gene expression while restraining progenitor proliferation; loss of either blocks red cell production, and GFI1B mutation causes a bleeding disorder with malformed platelets.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on stress-activated transcriptional signalling and its supporting membrane and metabolic machinery. [untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on control of cell survival and proliferation decisions during tissue growth and differentiation. Two hubs stand out: the retinoblastoma protein RB1, which restrains the G1/S transition by holding E2F-dependent transcription in check and whose loss underlies retinoblastoma and many sporadic cancers, and BCL2L1, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL2 family that guards mitochondrial outer membrane integrity and blocks cytochrome c release.

members: negative regulation of B cell differentiation

[untitled BTM module] Circulating monocytes find their way into tissue by reading chemokine gradients, and the two receptors that anchor this group, CCR2 and CX3CR1, are the pair that defines the classical and non-classical monocyte subsets and governs their recruitment to inflamed vessel walls, injured tissue and the brain, where they become macrophages or microglia. Loss or blockade of this axis limits atherosclerotic plaque myeloid influx and blunts inflammatory infiltration, which is why it is a longstanding drug target.

[untitled BTM module] Granulocyte development and activation is the theme here: a transcriptional core that commits myeloid progenitors to the neutrophil lineage, a cytokine receptor that drives their expansion, and signalling and cytoskeletal components that let mature cells respond. PU.1 and the retinoic acid receptor set and maintain myeloid identity, which is why blockade of retinoid signalling in promyelocytic leukaemia arrests cells short of maturity and why pharmacological retinoid treatment restores it.

[untitled BTM module] A mixed immune-expression module centred on mononuclear leukocyte identity and trafficking, combining chemokine receptors, GTPase-of-immunity-associated proteins and transcriptional regulators. Monocyte and macrophage recruitment to inflamed tissue depends on CCR2 and CX3CR1, whose ligands direct patrolling and infiltrating cells to vessel walls and injured sites; loss of this axis blunts inflammatory monocyte egress from bone marrow and reshapes atherosclerotic and neuroinflammatory disease.
